stemMd: The graphs $y=x^2$ and $y=2x+3$ intersect at two points. What is the greater $x$-coordinate?
explanationMd: Set the outputs equal: x²=2x+3, giving x²−2x−3=(x−3)(x+1)=0. The x-coordinates are 3 and −1; the greater is 3.

distractorRationale.a: This is the smaller intersection x-coordinate.
distractorRationale.b: This is the slope of the line, not an intersection.
distractorRationale.d: This is the y-coordinate corresponding to the greater x.
